body:
Two clarifications to make triage easier, and to state a limit on the claim above.

**This requires `enableDBStore: true`.** The counter is only read and published when the DB store is enabled:

```go
// service/init.go
if factory.SmfConfig.Configuration.EnableDbStore {
    smfContext.SetupSmfCollection()   // -> GetUniqueIdentity("smfCount") -> os.Setenv("SMF_COUNT", ...)
}
```

With `enableDBStore: false`, `SMF_COUNT` is never set, `smfCountStr` falls back to `"1"`, the offset is 0, and none of this occurs. The reproduction above assumes the DB store is on; the summary should have said so up front.

**The SMF must also be the allocator for it to surface.** Where the UPF advertises the UEIP feature, `ActivateUpLinkPdr` sets `CHV4` and the UPF allocates, so the SMF's local address is released and replaced in `HandlePfcpSessionEstablishmentResponse` — the stride never reaches the UE. In our deployment the SMF does not delegate (`UEIpAddr` goes out with `V4=true` and `CHV4=false`), so its own allocation is what the UE receives.

So the conditions are: DB store enabled, and the SMF allocating rather than the UPF. Both are ordinary configurations, but neither is universal, and it is worth knowing which deployments are exposed.

What we would still argue is a defect regardless of intent: **an address outside the configured pool is never a correct allocation.** Whatever the stride is meant to achieve, `IPAddrWithOffset` can leave `a.ipNetwork` entirely and the result is returned without an error. A bound check that fails loudly would have turned a silent one-way loss of connectivity into an obvious startup failure.

issue.title: upfadapter: Association Setup Response handler drops UP Function Features, so the SMF never learns the UPF can allocate UE IPs
issue.body:
## Summary

`pfcp/adapter/adapter.go`'s `HandlePfcpAssociationSetupResponse` records `UPFStatus`, `RecoveryTimeStamp` and `NHeartBeat` from the Association Setup Response, but never records the **UP Function Features** IE. The native handler in `pfcp/handler/handler.go` does.

The two are on mutually exclusive dispatch paths, so with `enableUPFAdapter: true` the SMF permanently believes the UPF supports no optional features — including UEIP.

## Why it matters

`UPFunctionFeatures` has exactly one assignment in the tree:

```go
// pfcp/handler/handler.go:375
if rsp.UPFunctionFeatures != nil {
    UPFunctionFeatures, err := ies.UnmarshalUserPlaneFunctionFeatures(rsp.UPFunctionFeatures.Payload)
    ...
    upf.UPFunctionFeatures = UPFunctionFeatures
}
```

That block has no counterpart in the adapter handler. Downstream:

```go
// context/upf.go:602
func (upf *UPF) IsUpfSupportUeIpAddrAlloc() bool {
    if upf.UPFunctionFeatures != nil &&
        (upf.UPFunctionFeatures.SupportedFeatures1&UpFunctionFeatures1Ueip) == UpFunctionFeatures1Ueip {

// context/datapath.go:591
if dpNode.UPF.IsUpfSupportUeIpAddrAlloc() {
    ueIpAddr.CHV4 = true          // ask the UPF to allocate
} else {
    ueIpAddr.V4 = true            // use the SMF's own allocation
    ueIpAddr.Ipv4Address = smContext.PDUAddress.Ip.To4()
}
```

So in adapter mode `CHV4` is never set, the UPF is never asked to allocate, and the SMF's local allocator is authoritative — even when the UPF is explicitly configured to allocate. Both handlers contain the `PDUAddress.UpfProvided = true` path that consumes a UPF-allocated address, but in adapter mode nothing can ever cause one to be sent, so that code is unreachable.

## Observed

UPF configured with `enable_ue_ip_alloc: true`, which makes it advertise the UEIP bit (`pfcpiface/messages_conn.go:113`, `pfcpiface/utils.go:31`). SMF running with the adapter:

```
INFO  adapter/adapter.go:215  handle PFCP Association Setup Response with NodeID[10.43.79.49]
```

and the resulting PDR carries the SMF's own address with `CHV4` clear:

```
UEIpAddr:[&{192.168.100.3 <nil> false true false false false ...}]
                          V6=f  V4=t              CHV4=f
```

The same deployment with the native PFCP path sets `CHV4` and the UPF allocates.

## Dispatch paths, for reference

Adapter responses do not go through `pfcp.Dispatch`; they arrive synchronously and are routed by `HandleAdapterPfcpRsp`:

```go
// pfcp/adapter/adapter.go:139
func HandleAdapterPfcpRsp(pfcpMsg message.Message, evtData *udp.PfcpEventData) error {
    switch pfcpMsg.MessageType() {
    case message.MsgTypeAssociationSetupResponse:
        HandlePfcpAssociationSetupResponse(&msg)   // adapter's own, no UPFunctionFeatures
```

Confirmed on `upstream/main`: `pfcp/adapter/adapter.go` has 0 references to `UPFunctionFeatures`; `pfcp/handler/handler.go` has 5.

## Suggested fix

Record the IE in the adapter handler as the native one does. The parse is already factored into `ies.UnmarshalUserPlaneFunctionFeatures`, so it is the same handful of lines.

More generally, the two association-response handlers have drifted, and any feature negotiated at association time will be silently absent in adapter mode. It may be worth extracting the shared post-accept body so the two paths cannot diverge again — the `UpfProvided` block is already duplicated verbatim between them.

## Related

This is the mechanism that makes #621 reachable in practice: because the SMF is forced to be the allocator in adapter mode, the unbounded `(SMF_COUNT-1)*5000` stride described there is what the UE actually receives.

body:
Correcting my previous comment, which named the second condition without its cause.

I wrote that the stride only surfaces when "the SMF is the allocator rather than the UPF", and left that as a deployment property. It is not — it has a specific mechanism, and I have since filed it as #622.

In `enableUPFAdapter: true` deployments the SMF **cannot** be anything but the allocator, because the adapter's Association Setup Response handler never records the UP Function Features IE. `IsUpfSupportUeIpAddrAlloc()` therefore always returns false, `CHV4` is never set, and the UPF is never asked to allocate — regardless of it being configured to, and regardless of it advertising the capability.

So the exposure is narrower and sharper than "some deployments":

- `enableDBStore: true` — otherwise `SMF_COUNT` is unset and the offset is 0
- **and** either `enableUPFAdapter: true` (where #622 forces local allocation unconditionally), or a UPF that does not advertise UEIP

The second bullet is worth stating that way because the natural mitigation for this issue — "let the UPF allocate" — does not work in adapter mode. Both need fixing, and #622 is the cheaper of the two.

I should also withdraw the framing in my original report that this is purely a function of restart count. Restart count determines the *magnitude* of the offset; whether the offset reaches the UE at all is determined by #622.
